assertions.title: Netflix ROI frames the page as a committee-grade content allocation board

steps.action: Open /projects/netflix-roi on the shared localhost:3501 runtime
steps.expected: Netflix ROI hero and BLUF frame acquisition-vs-retention tradeoffs and committee decision posture
steps.observed: Hero shows 'Investment Committee Room', 'Acquisition vs retention split', 'Capital allocation frontier', and H1 'Netflix ROI Autopsy: capital committee decision deck'.

steps.expected: BLUF explains title-level slate economics and modeled committee framing
steps.observed: BLUF includes the business question about subscriber acquisition vs retention, a bottom line about synthetic control estimates and Pareto frontier, and 'Portfolio allocation output: Acquisition vs retention frontier'.

assertions.title: Netflix controls update modeled frontier and title-ranking outputs

steps.action: Inspect the route for interactive controls affecting budget, buzz, acclaim, retention, or decay
steps.expected: Visible simulator controls are available for user manipulation
steps.observed: The page only exposed evidence-rail filter buttons ('all', 'shock', 'anomaly', 'inflection', 'recommendation'). The page text states 'Interactive controls are loading' and 'Incoming modules: Scenario sliders, stress charts, and recommendation console.'

steps.action: Attempt interaction through the visible Netflix route controls
steps.expected: Selected-title details plus at least two downstream outputs update visibly
steps.observed: No budget/buzz/acclaim/retention/decay controls were present, and the required selected-title/detail-output update could not be produced. Clicking visible controls did not surface the missing simulator module in the validated state.

evidence.network: Route HTML served successfully from localhost:3501, but no separate client request activity was captured by agent-browser during the failed control validation.

assertions.issues: Required simulator inputs and downstream recommendation controls were not rendered in the tested production-like route state; the route remained in an 'Interactive controls are loading' placeholder state.

assertions.title: Netflix route translates analysis into interpretable recommendation language

steps.action: Inspect the decision surface for recommendation outputs
steps.expected: The route exposes predicted adds, retention months, greenlight score, capital recommendation, and supporting evidence
steps.observed: The visible page showed BLUF, trust detail, frontier summary, retention lift, best net contribution, and the committee evidence rail, but not the required recommendation packet metrics.

steps.action: Search visible page text for required recommendation fields
steps.expected: Required recommendation labels are present and inspectable
steps.observed: Visible text did not include 'predicted adds', 'retention months', 'greenlight score', or 'capital recommendation'; only placeholder text referenced an incoming recommendation console.

assertions.issues: The route did not expose the required interpretable recommendation metrics in the real user surface; only a placeholder indicated that the recommendation console was still loading/incoming.

assertions.title: Netflix recommendation outputs remain explicitly modeled

steps.action: Inspect the top summary and trust framing
steps.expected: Modeled/decision-aid framing stays visible and does not present title economics as direct observed truth
steps.observed: The BLUF explicitly labels the route 'MODELED · Synthetic content panel + frontier optimizer' and states 'Limitation: Title economics are synthetic and intended for scenario stress testing only.'

steps.action: Inspect trust/provenance and assumptions entry points
steps.expected: Trust and assumption surfaces reinforce modeled framing
steps.observed: The page shows 'Trust, provenance & current run' plus 'Assumptions, limits & swap path', and trust detail distinguishes real feeds from unavailable contextual feeds while keeping modeled route framing explicit.

assertions.title: Netflix loading or route failures remain recoverable

steps.expected: A Netflix-specific loading state with visible recovery path appears
steps.observed: The route rendered the same normal page content as the baseline route; no route-specific loading state or recovery affordance was surfaced.

steps.expected: A Netflix-specific error state with retry or return-to-projects recovery appears
steps.observed: The route again rendered the same normal page content, so no route-level error or recovery UI could be honestly verified.

evidence.network: GET /projects/netflix-roi?routeProbe=loading -> route rendered normally; GET /projects/netflix-roi?routeProbe=error -> route rendered normally

assertions.issues: Supported recoverability probes did not trigger a distinct loading or failure surface on the healthy runtime, so recoverability could not be verified through the real user surface.

frictions.description: The Netflix route exposed only the first interactive chapter and a placeholder for the allocation committee module during this validation run.
frictions.resolution: Waited, rescrolled, reloaded the route, increased viewport size, and retried visible interactions, but the simulator controls and recommendation console never rendered.

frictions.description: The supported routeProbe URLs for Netflix ROI rendered the same normal route content instead of a distinct loading/error state.
frictions.resolution: Captured screenshots for both probe URLs and marked recoverability validation blocked rather than guessing.

blockers.description: The production-like Netflix ROI route did not surface the required simulator/recommendation module during validation, preventing honest verification of control-driven updates and recommendation packet outputs.
blockers.quickFixAttempted: Reloaded the route, waited additional time, changed viewport, rescrolled, and retried visible control interaction; the missing module still did not render.

blockers.description: Route-level loading/error recoverability probes for Netflix ROI did not produce a distinguishable loading or error state on the healthy runtime.
blockers.quickFixAttempted: Tested both supported probe URLs directly on localhost:3501 and compared the rendered content to the baseline route; all rendered the same normal page.

summary: Tested 5 Netflix ROI assertions on localhost:3501: 2 passed, 2 failed, and 1 was blocked. The route convincingly frames a modeled committee-grade Netflix ROI analysis and keeps modeled/synthetic trust language explicit, but the production-like surface did not render the expected allocation committee simulator or recommendation packet, and supported recoverability probes did not surface a distinct loading/error state.
